newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Key session on global telecom pact delayed.
newsitem.headline: Key session on global telecom pact delayed.

text.p: Trade officials said a key session to assess chances of a global pact on basic telecommunications had been postponed by several hours to late on Friday.
The meeting of telecoms negotiators at the World Trade Organisation had originally been set for 2.30 p.m. (1330 GMT), but will now take place at 7.30 p.m. (1830 GMT). they said.
Deadline for agreement on a deal is midnight in Geneva (2300 GMT) on February 15.
Trade diplomats said the delay in calling Friday's session of the WTO telecoms working group would give more time for the presently 61 countries in the talks to improve offers.
The United States has been making it clear it wants better openings to domestic markets in many countries for international competition before it can agree to a pact.
Trade sources said a total of 61 countries had now made offers, covering some 93 per cent of world basic telecoms revenue of over $600 billion annually.
Latest to come in on Friday was Bangladesh, following Papua-New Guinea and Brunei who presented their first-ever offers in the talks on Thursday.
Trade diplomats said revised offers have been presented by South Korea and Mexico, both of whom had been signalled by the United States as having presented insufficient packages.
There was no comment from U.S. officials in Geneva on their latest assessment of prospects for a deal. But one source said the Washington team was deep in talks with trading partners.
